title: When the Thorn Burns
premise: Cyrus Crane, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a charm-seller in the magic-hating city of Vell, discovers their face in a century-old prophecy book that names them the 'Thorn' who will either save or doom the last dragon. Hunted by the Inquisitor's Guild and bound to a prophecy they never chose, Cyrus must ally with a disgraced dragon-keeper and a traitor priestess to find the Door—a passage out of Ashkarin, a country that was erased from maps and memory after its fall. As the last dragon-fire gutters toward extinction, Cyrus learns that every use of their storm-magic burns a year of someone else's life, forcing them to weigh survival against love. In the end, Cyrus opens the Door not to escape but to release the dragon's fire back into the world, sacrificing their own magic—and nearly their life—to break the prophecy, choosing a small, mortal love over power.
about_author: Mirabel Nakamura is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing extinct nations before turning to fiction, a career that left her obsessed with borders, memory, and what survives erasure. She writes fantasy about people who would rather be forgotten than chosen.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: Cyrus sells a luck-charm to a frightened widow in Vell's night market, concealing the storm that crackles under their skin. POV: Cyrus. Beat: weary routine masking loneliness; establishes the city's fear of magic and Cyrus's careful invisibility.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't
chapters.summary: A charming stranger named Wren buys a protection charm and asks Cyrus to dinner; Cyrus, starved for connection, says yes against every instinct. POV: Cyrus. Beat: fragile hope, first crack in isolation.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Grief
chapters.summary: Wren reveals herself as an archivist and shows Cyrus a prophecy book from fallen Ashkarin—where a figure with Cyrus's exact scarred hands is named the Thorn. POV: Cyrus. Beat: dread blooming through wonder.

chapters.title: What the Guild Burns
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Halvard Voss interrogates a charm-seller in the public square; Cyrus watches from the crowd, recognizing the man whose testimony exiled them twelve years ago. POV: alternating Cyrus/Voss. Beat: cold terror; the hunt has begun.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Magics
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Cyrus calls a storm to save a drowning village and is branded a heretic, exiled while their lover Sefa chooses duty over them. POV: Cyrus. Beat: grief explained; why love feels like a trap.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Embers
chapters.summary: Wren leads Cyrus to Bren, a drunk disgraced dragon-keeper who guards a dying coal he claims is the last dragon's heart-flame. POV: Bren. Beat: bitter humor hiding despair; reluctant alliance formed.

chapters.title: Ashkarin Was Here
chapters.summary: Bren explains that Ashkarin didn't just fall—it was unmade, erased from records and minds, and the Door out of it still exists somewhere beneath Vell. POV: Bren. Beat: vertigo of impossible history; quest defined.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Voss finds Cyrus's market stall burned and riddled with guild seals; he interrogates Wren's colleagues, closing in. POV: Voss. Beat: menace rising; Voss believes killing the Thorn will restore his ruined name.

chapters.title: Storms Have a Price
chapters.summary: Attacked by guild hunters, Cyrus unleashes real storm-magic to escape—and watches a stranger in the street collapse, aged years in seconds. POV: Cyrus. Beat: horror at the cost; the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Sefa's Shadow
chapters.summary: Cyrus learns Sefa now serves on the Inquisitor's Council—the lover who chose duty may be hunting them personally. POV: Cyrus. Beat: heartbreak weaponized into urgency.

chapters.title: The Priestess Who Lied
chapters.summary: They seek Ilyra, a traitor priestess of the erased Ashkarin faith, who confirms the Door exists but warns the prophecy demands the Thorn burn. POV: Ilyra. Beat: ambiguous ally; faith versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: Under the City's Skin
chapters.summary: Descending through Vell's drowned catacombs, the group finds walls inscribed in a language only Cyrus can read—the storm-caller's gift is also a key. POV: Cyrus. Beat: eerie wonder; destiny tightening.

chapters.title: Wren's Honest Lie
chapters.summary: Cyrus catches Wren copying the prophecy pages for a buyer; she admits she sought him out deliberately—he was her assignment all along. POV: Wren. Beat: betrayal shattering budding trust and love.

chapters.title: The Buyer Below
chapters.summary: Wren's buyer is revealed: a cabal of nobles who want the dragon's fire to fuel their own ascension, proving power corrupts even the powerless. POV: Wren. Beat: moral collapse; Wren realizes what she's unleashed.

chapters.title: Coal and Breath
chapters.summary: The ember flares and speaks in dreams: the dragon, Yssara, shows Cyrus visions of Ashkarin alive—its people, its storms, its murder. POV: Cyrus. Beat: awe and mourning; stakes become personal and historical.

chapters.title: Council of Ashes
chapters.summary: Sefa argues before the Council that the Thorn should be captured, not killed—but Voss outmaneuvers her, and she is ordered to lead the hunt. POV: Sefa. Beat: duty crushing conscience; old wound reopened.

chapters.title: The Toll Road
chapters.summary: Fleeing through the salt flats, the group shelters with refugees from erased borderlands who still whisper Ashkarin's name; Cyrus performs small healing charms, spending strangers' years unknowingly. POV: Bren. Beat: tenderness amid decay; Bren confronts his own failures.

chapters.title: Ilyra's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilyra offers to shield Cyrus from the prophecy's burning clause—if Cyrus gives her the storm-magic itself. POV: Ilyra. Beat: temptation; power offered as salvation and corruption at once.

chapters.title: Refusal in the Rain
chapters.summary: Cyrus refuses Ilyra and instead teaches Wren to anchor his storms so no one else pays the price—an act of trust that mends their broken bond. POV: Cyrus. Beat: love rebuilt on honesty rather than need.

chapters.title: Voss Ascendant
chapters.summary: Voss seizes control of the Guild, declaring martial law; Vell's streets fill with pyres. He publicly brands Cyrus the cause of every plague since the exile. POV: Voss. Beat: tyranny crystallizing; the city turns on its own.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: Beneath a flooded temple, the group finds the true map of Ashkarin—and learns the Door opens only when the last dragon-fire gutters out, not before. POV: Wren. Beat: cruel irony; escape requires near-extinction.

chapters.title: Sefa at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Sefa corners Cyrus alone and, instead of arresting him, begs him to run—twelve years of regret spilling out. POV: Sefa. Beat: aching what-if; love against duty embodied in one scene.

chapters.title: The Cabal Moves
chapters.summary: The noble cabal steals the ember-heart from Bren, leaving him hollow; without it, Yssara begins to die in earnest. POV: Bren. Beat: devastation; Bren's purpose stripped away.

chapters.title: Chase Through the Pyre City
chapters.summary: A running battle across burning Vell as the group pursues the cabal; Cyrus must choose between saving civilians and catching the thieves—and saves the people. POV: Cyrus. Beat: character defining choice; survival ethic overturned.

chapters.title: Ilyra's True Face
chapters.summary: Ilyra betrays the group to the cabal, revealing she intends to consume the dragon-fire herself and resurrect Ashkarin as its god-queen. POV: Ilyra. Beat: corruption complete; the theme's dark mirror.

chapters.title: Guttering
chapters.summary: Yssara's fire dims visibly across the sky; crops fail, tides stutter. The world itself begins forgetting how to be warm. POV: Cyrus. Beat: apocalyptic quiet; time running out.

chapters.title: The Prophecy Reread
chapters.summary: Wren deciphers the prophecy's final line correctly at last: the Thorn doesn't burn—the Thorn chooses what burns. The book was a warning, not a sentence. POV: Wren. Beat: revelation; agency reclaimed from fate.

chapters.title: Prison of Salt and Iron
chapters.summary: Captured by Voss, Cyrus is caged beside Sefa, now arrested for treason; in the dark they finally speak honestly about the day she let him be exiled. POV: alternating. Beat: catharsis; forgiveness without reconciliation.

chapters.title: Voss's Coronation
chapters.summary: Voss plans to execute the Thorn publicly and claim the dragon-fire for the Guild, staging himself as savior. POV: Voss. Beat: hubris at its peak; the stage set for downfall.

chapters.title: The Breaking of Bren
chapters.summary: Bren sacrifices himself to sabotage the execution pyre, buying Cyrus minutes and passing the keeper's oath to Wren. POV: Bren. Beat: tragic heroism; the mentor's last lesson.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Square
chapters.summary: Before thousands, Cyrus calls the greatest storm of their life—with Wren anchoring it, no one pays the toll. Voss's authority shatters as the crowd sees magic used to protect, not harm. POV: Cyrus. Beat: triumph and exposure; invisibility ends forever.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath
chapters.summary: Guided by Sefa's knowledge of the Guild tunnels, the survivors reach the Door of erased Ashkarin as Ilyra and the cabal converge with the stolen ember. POV: Sefa. Beat: breathless convergence; every thread arriving at one threshold.

chapters.title: Ilyra Ascending
chapters.summary: Ilyra feeds the ember into herself and begins transforming into something vast and burning—a god being born from stolen fire. POV: Ilyra. Beat: body horror and grandeur; power's final corruption.

chapters.title: What the Thorn Chooses
chapters.summary: Understanding the prophecy at last, Cyrus seizes the ember from Ilyra's unraveling form and chooses what burns: not the dragon, not the world, but his own exile-brand and the storm-magic bound to it. POV: Cyrus. Beat: climax; sacrifice as authorship of fate.

chapters.title: Fire Returns to the Sky
chapters.summary: Yssara rises whole from the Door, her fire restored, and unmakes Ilyra's half-born divinity; Ashkarin's name returns to every map and mind in the country. POV: Cyrus. Beat: restoration; the erased remembered.

chapters.title: The Cost Counted
chapters.summary: Magicless and half-dead, Cyrus wakes in Wren's arms; Sefa stands guard, having finally chosen love—not for Cyrus, but for the person she wants to become. POV: Wren. Beat: tender aftermath; grief and gratitude entwined.

chapters.title: Trials and Testimonies
chapters.summary: Voss faces the Council he once ruled; Sefa testifies against him, ending her duty to the Guild and beginning her duty to the truth. POV: Sefa. Beat: justice without vengeance; closure for the antagonist thread.

chapters.title: Ashkarin Remembers
chapters.summary: The restored nation's first free festival fills Vell; Cyrus, anonymous again but by choice this time, sells nothing and simply belongs. POV: Cyrus. Beat: quiet joy; identity rebuilt beyond exile and prophecy alike.

chapters.title: A Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Yssara offers Cyrus a place among dragon-keepers—or a plain life; Cyrus chooses Wren, a small house, and seasons that arrive on time. POV: Cyrus. Beat: love chosen freely over power and destiny both.

chapters.title: When the Thorn Burns
chapters.summary: Years later, Cyrus plants a rosebush where the pyre once stood; when it blooms through old ash, the prophecy book's last page fades blank. POV: Cyrus. Beat: resolution; the future unwritten, warm, and theirs.
